mainTopic: Mourning before a רגל, burial work on חול המועד, and why weddings are forbidden on חול המועד.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. It gives a second reason not to lament the dead within thirty days before a רגל: grief stays in the heart for thirty days. The two reasons give different results when a eulogizer works for free. A new משנה then forbids digging new כוכין and קברות on חול המועד, but allows adjusting existing כוכין, making a laundry pond, and making a coffin when the body is in the courtyard. The גמרא defines these terms and links the coffin rule to a ברייתא about the needs of the dead. A second משנה forbids weddings and יבום on חול המועד because of the joy, and also covers cosmetics, sewing, and bed cords. The גמרא asks why joy should be a problem on a festival. It gives four answers: not mixing joys, the wedding pushing aside the festival's joy (traced to רב and ושמחת בחגך), the effort involved, and the risk that people would delay פריה ורביה. A challenge from a ברייתא begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The second reason: the dead is remembered for thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes giving its second reason for not lamenting the dead within thirty days before a רגל: the pain of a death stays in the heart for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because a dead person is not forgotten from the heart for thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation it started before this section. It gives a second reason for the rule that you should not stir up mourning for your dead within thirty days before a רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that grief stays fresh for thirty days. If you hold a הספד within thirty days of the רגל, the sadness will still be there on the יום טוב itself, and that harms the festival joy. This reason looks at the mourner's feelings, not at money.

keyTerms.meaning: A eulogy or lament for the dead

phrases.english: Because the dead person is not forgotten
from the heart for thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין הַמֵּת מִשְׁתַּכֵּחַ מִן הַלֵּב שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a discussion begun before this section, offering a second reason for the rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Grief lasts thirty days, so a הספד within thirty days of the רגל would carry sadness into the festival.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a practical case where the two reasons would lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now has two reasons for the same rule, so it asks whether there is any case where they lead to different results. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two reasons are given for one rule, the גמרא often looks for a case that only one of them covers. That shows the two reasons are really different ideas.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: Between the two reasons: the one given earlier (about money set aside for the festival) and the one just stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the second reason differs in practice from the first.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons lead to different results.

steps.title: A eulogizer who works for free
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up when the eulogizer does not charge. The money worry falls away, but the grief worry remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when he does it for free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons split when the person giving the eulogy works for free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no money is spent, the reason about using up festival money no longer applies. The reason about grief staying in the heart for thirty days still applies. So by the second reason the הספד would still be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: The two reasons split over a free eulogizer. The money concern disappears, but the grief concern stays.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he does it for free.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person giving the eulogy, who takes no payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A free eulogy: no money concern, but the grief concern still applies.

steps.title: משנה: graves, crypts, a laundry pond, and a coffin on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids digging new כוכין and קברות on חול המועד. It allows adjusting existing כוכין, making a laundry pond, and making a coffin when the dead body is in the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not dig crypts or graves on the festival, but one may adjust crypts on the festival. One may make a laundry pond on the festival, and a coffin when the dead body is in the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists which kinds of burial-related work are forbidden on חול המועד and which are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Digging brand-new burial places is forbidden. Fixing up an existing כוך so it fits is allowed. A coffin may be made when the body is right there in the courtyard, because then the work is clearly for the dead person.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may not dig crypts and graves on the festival,
phrases.notes: 'The festival' here means חול המועד, the middle days of the festival.

phrases.english: but one may adjust the crypts on the festival.
And one may make a pond on the festival,
and a coffin, when it is with the dead body in the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Digging new כוכין and קברות is forbidden. Adjusting existing כוכין, making a pond, and making a coffin when the body is in the courtyard are allowed.

steps.title: רבי יהודה is stricter about the coffin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids making the coffin unless the boards are already with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה forbids it unless he has boards with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first part of the משנה about the coffin and adds a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, having the body in the courtyard is not enough. He allows making a coffin only if the boards are already there, so less work is needed on חול המועד.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda forbids it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ עִמּוֹ נְסָרִים.
phrases.english: unless he has boards with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ עִמּוֹ נְסָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting, stricter view on the coffin ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A coffin may be made only if the boards are already on hand.

steps.title: What are כוכין and what are קברות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the definitions of the two kinds of burial places named in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are crypts and what are graves?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts on the משנה by asking what exactly כוכין and קברות are and how they differ. This sets up רב יהודה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names both terms without explaining them, so the גמרא wants clear definitions.

keyTerms.meaning: The תלמוד's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What are crypts and what are graves?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for definitions of terms in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definitions of כוכין and קברות.

steps.title: רב יהודה: כוכין are dug, קברות are built
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that כוכין are made by digging, and קברות are made by building.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: crypts are made by digging, and graves by building.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by explaining how each kind of burial place is made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is in how they are made. A כוך is dug out of the ground or rock. A קבר here is something built up. The משנה forbids both on חול המועד.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Crypts are by digging,
and graves are by building.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כוכין are dug, and קברות are built.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same definitions as רב יהודה, word for word.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: these are crypts and these are graves. Crypts are by digging, and graves are by building.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב יהודה's definitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches רב יהודה exactly, so his explanation is backed by an earlier teaching and is not just his own opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא
A teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: כוכין are dug and קברות are built. רב יהודה says this and a ברייתא agrees.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ הֵן כּוּכִין וְאֵלּוּ הֵן קְבָרוֹת,
phrases.english: These are crypts and these are graves:
crypts are by digging,
and graves are by building.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's definitions of כוכין and קברות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording.

steps.title: How does one adjust a כוך?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's permission to adjust כוכין and asks what adjusting means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'But one may adjust the crypts.' How does one adjust them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next phrase of the משנה and asks what kind of adjusting is allowed. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows 'adjusting' a כוך but does not say what that work is. The גמרא wants to know exactly what is permitted.

phrases.english: 'But one may adjust the crypts.'
How does one adjust them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What work counts as adjusting a כוך.

steps.title: רב יהודה: if it is too long, he shortens it
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that adjusting means shortening a כוך that is too long.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: if it was long, he shortens it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers: adjusting means making a כוך that is too long shorter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב יהודה's example the work fixes an existing כוך so it fits, instead of creating a new one. That is why it is allowed on חול המועד.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
If it was long, he shortens it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה שֶׁאִם הָיָה אָרוֹךְ מְקַצְּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Adjusting means shortening a כוך that is too long.

steps.title: A ברייתא: he lengthens it and widens it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes adjusting as lengthening and widening the כוך.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: he lengthens it and widens it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that describes adjusting the other way: making the כוך longer and wider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה spoke of shortening. The ברייתא speaks of lengthening and widening. Either way, adjusting means changing the size of an existing כוך so it fits the body.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: 'Adjusting' a כוך means changing the size of an existing one so it fits: shortening (רב יהודה) or lengthening and widening (the ברייתא). Digging a brand-new one is not allowed.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
He lengthens it and widens it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another description of adjusting, next to רב יהודה's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Adjusting includes lengthening and widening the כוך.

steps.title: What is a laundry pond?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's permission to make a נברכת and asks what that word means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may make a נברכת.' What is a נברכת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the משנה and asks for the meaning of an unfamiliar word. This sets up the next step, where רב יהודה answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows a נברכת during חול המועד but never defines it. Before the rule can be understood, we need to know what object is being made.

keyTerms.meaning: A pool or pond used for washing clothes
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: 'And one may make a laundry pond, etc.'
What is a laundry pond?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the כוכין discussion to the next item in the משנה.

steps.title: רב יהודה: it is a ditch
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that a נברכת is a בקיע, a ditch dug for washing clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: this is a ditch.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by saying a נברכת is the same thing as a בקיע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה treats the two words as two names for one thing, a laundry ditch. That claim is what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A ditch dug in the ground, here one used for laundry

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is a ditch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A נברכת is a בקיע, a laundry ditch.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists them as two things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה from a ברייתא that mentions נברכת and בקיע separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'the pond and the ditch.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה's answer. A ברייתא lists the two words side by side, which suggests they are different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both words meant the same thing, the ברייתא would not need to list both. Naming them separately seems to show they are not identical.

phrases.english: But it was taught: The pond and the ditch!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that נברכת equals בקיע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lists both words, so they must be two different things.

steps.title: A pond and a small pond
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רב כהנא) answers that the two are the same kind of thing and differ only in size.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, and some say it was רב כהנא: a pond and a small pond.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי (some say רב כהנא) defends רב יהודה. Both words describe a laundry pool, but one is big and one is small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists both because they differ in size, not in kind. So רב יהודה was right that a נברכת is basically a ditch for washing. The ברייתא simply separates the larger one from the smaller one.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'son of a pond', meaning a small pond

steps.whatToRemember: נברכת and בקיע are the same kind of laundry pool; they differ only in size.

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say it was Rav Kahana:
A pond and a small pond.
phrases.notes: The bigger one is the נברכת, and the smaller one is the בקיע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fine distinction: same kind of thing, different size
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing both words means they are totally different things.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are the same kind of pool; the ברייתא lists both because one is large and one is small.

steps.title: The coffin rule matches a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's permission to make a coffin and notes that a ברייתא teaches the same rule, along with other needs of the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And a coffin, when the dead body is in the courtyard.' We already learned in the משנה what the רבנן taught in a ברייתא: one may do all the needs of the dead during the festival. One may cut his hair, wash his clothing, and make him a coffin from boards that were already cut before the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the משנה's rule about making a coffin agrees with a ברייתא. The ברייתא lists everything that may be done for a dead person during חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows caring for the dead during the festival, but it limits the coffin to boards that were already cut before יום טוב. This shows that the coffin may be put together, but the bigger work of cutting new boards is not allowed, at least according to the first opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The needs of the dead (preparing him for burial)

phrases.english: 'And a coffin, when he is with the dead body in the courtyard.'
We already learned this, as the Rabbis taught:
One may do all the needs of the dead.
One may cut his hair for him,
and one may wash his clothing for him,
and one may make him a coffin from boards
that were cut before the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the משנה, the coffin.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's permission to make a coffin during חול המועד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the needs of the dead that may be done during the festival.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: even cutting boards privately
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows even bringing wood and cutting boards, as long as it is done privately at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: one may even bring wood and cut it into boards discreetly inside his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second, more lenient opinion. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows cutting new boards for the coffin, but only in private.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion allowed only boards that were already cut. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes further and allows the cutting itself. He requires it to be done privately so it does not look like ordinary weekday work in public.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone allows making a coffin during the festival. They disagree only about whether new boards may be cut, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows it in private.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One may even bring wood and saw it
privately, inside his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף מְבִיאִין עֵצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood may be cut into coffin boards during the festival if it is done privately at home.

steps.title: No weddings or levirate marriage on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה forbids marrying any woman, or doing יבום, during חול המועד because of the great joy involved, but it allows remarrying a divorced wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not marry women during the festival, neither virgins nor widows, and one may not do יבום, because it is a joy for him. But he may remarry his divorced wife.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It forbids getting married during חול המועד, whether to a virgin or a widow, and forbids יבום. It allows remarrying one's own divorced wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says the wedding is 'a joy for him.' It does not explain why that should matter on a festival, and the גמרא will ask exactly this in step 22. Remarrying a divorcée is allowed because it is not the same level of new joy.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing יבום, marrying a brother's childless widow

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה names joy as its reason. But the גמרא gives several explanations of the ban, and not all of them are about joy: עולא (step 26) says it is because of the work of preparing a wedding.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not marry women during the festival,
not virgins and not widows,
and one may not do levirate marriage,
because it is a joy for him.
But he may take back his divorced wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No marriage or יבום during חול המועד because of the joy; remarrying a divorced wife is allowed.

steps.title: Women's cosmetics on the festival
steps.stepSummary: A woman may do her beauty treatments during חול המועד, but רבי יהודה forbids applying lime because it makes her look bad for a while.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a woman may do her beauty treatments during the festival. רבי יהודה says: she may not apply lime, because it is a disgrace to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה allows a woman's cosmetic care during חול המועד. רבי יהודה makes an exception for lime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beauty treatments add to her enjoyment of the festival, so they are allowed. Lime makes her look unattractive until it is peeled off, so for now it causes distress instead of joy, and רבי יהודה forbids it.

phrases.english: And a woman may do her beauty treatments during the festival.
Rabbi Yehuda says: She may not apply lime,
because it is a disgrace for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with another festival rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cosmetics are allowed during חול המועד; רבי יהודה forbids lime because it disfigures her for a time.

steps.title: Sewing: amateur versus professional
steps.stepSummary: An ordinary person may sew normally, but a skilled tailor may only make loose, temporary stitches.
steps.simpleTranslation: An ordinary person sews in his normal way, but a craftsman makes only loose, temporary stitches.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה allows sewing during חול המועד but treats a professional differently from an amateur.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An amateur's normal sewing is simple work, so it is allowed. A professional's normal sewing is real skilled work, so he must sew in an unusual, temporary way.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person, not a professional
Makes long, loose stitches, like basting

phrases.english: An ordinary person sews in his usual way,
and the craftsman makes loose stitches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה continues with another kind of work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An amateur sews normally; a professional may only sew loose, temporary stitches.

steps.title: Bed cords: weaving or only tightening
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion allows weaving the cords of a bed frame; רבי יוסי allows only tightening them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may weave the cords of beds. רבי יוסי says: one may only tighten them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה allows weaving the ropes of a bed frame during חול המועד. רבי יוסי allows only tightening ropes that are already there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion allows the full job of weaving the cords. רבי יוסי is stricter and allows only the smaller fix of tightening loose cords.

keyTerms.meaning: Weaving the ropes across a bed frame
Tightening ropes that are already in place

phrases.english: And one may weave the cords of the beds,
Rabbi Yosei says: One may only tighten them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה continues with another household repair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weaving bed cords is allowed; רבי יוסי allows only tightening them.

steps.title: What is wrong with joy on a festival?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the joy of a wedding should be a reason to forbid it, since a festival is a time for joy anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And if it is a joy for him, what of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking about the reason the משנה gave. If marrying makes a person happy, why is that bad on a festival?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbade weddings on חול המועד "because it is a joy for him." That sounds strange, because the festival itself is a time of joy. So the גמרא asks for the real logic behind the rule, and the next steps give several answers.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
And if it is a joy for him,
phrases.notes: This quotes the reason the משנה gave in step 18 for forbidding weddings on חול המועד.

phrases.english: what of it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי שִׂמְחָה הִיא לוֹ, מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the משנה's ban on marrying during חול המועד (step 18).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why should the joy of a wedding be a reason to forbid it during a festival, which is itself a time of joy?

steps.title: First answer: do not mix one joy with another
steps.stepSummary: Several אמוראים say weddings are forbidden on the festival because we do not mix one joy with another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, and so too רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא (and some say רבי אלעזר said it in the name of רבי חנינא): because we do not mix one joy with another joy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer. The festival's joy and the wedding's joy should each be celebrated on their own, not combined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not joy itself. The problem is combining two separate joys, so that neither one gets its full celebration. The long chain of names shows that this reason was passed down by several teachers.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not mix one joy with another joy

steps.whatToRemember: Reason #1: each joy deserves its own celebration, so a wedding should not be folded into the festival.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא,
phrases.english: and so too Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Oshaya said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: and some say: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Ḥanina said:
because one may not mix joy with joy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two joys may not be combined. The wedding and the festival each need their own celebration.

steps.title: Second answer: he would leave the festival's joy for his wife's joy
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא says the problem is that the groom would put aside the festival's joy and focus on his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: because he leaves the joy of the festival and busies himself with the joy of his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. A new groom would be so focused on his wife that the festival's joy would be pushed aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer is worried about mixing two joys. This answer is worried that the wedding joy will take over and the festival's joy will be lost. The focus is on protecting the festival.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
phrases.notes: Some versions add the word רב here; that's why it's in square brackets.

phrases.english: because he leaves the joy of the festival
and busies himself with the joy of his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ שִׂמְחַת הָרֶגֶל וְעוֹסֵק בְּשִׂמְחַת אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wedding joy would push aside the festival joy.

steps.title: אביי shows this answer comes from רב and a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב יוסף that רבה בר רב הונא's reason is really רב's, learned from the פסוק "ושמחת בחגך": rejoice in your festival, not in your wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: this teaching of רבה בר רב הונא is really רב's. For רב דניאל בר קטינא said in the name of רב: From where do we know that one does not marry during the festival? The פסוק says "And you shall rejoice in your festival." In your festival, and not in your wife.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds support to the second answer. He shows it goes back to רב, who learned it from a פסוק in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "בחגך" (in your festival) is read as a limit. Your joy should be in the festival itself, not in something else like a new wife. This gives רבה בר רב הונא's reason a source in the תורה, not just logic.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall rejoice in your festival (דברים 16:14)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not giving a new, third reason. He is showing that the second reason (step 24) is the same as רב's teaching, now with a פסוק behind it.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
This statement of Rabba bar Rav Huna —
is Rav's.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב דָּנִיאֵל בַּר קַטִּינָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: For Rav Daniel bar Ketina said that Rav said:
From where do we know that one does not marry women on the festival?
As it says: "And you shall rejoice in your festival,"
"in your festival" — and not in your wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא דְּרַב הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 24's reason by tracing it to רב and a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבה בר רב הונא's reason that the wedding joy pushes aside the festival joy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's reading of "ושמחת בחגך": rejoice in your festival and not in your wife.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that at least one reason for the ban has a basis in a פסוק, not only in logic.

steps.title: Third answer: too much work
steps.stepSummary: עולא says weddings are forbidden because of the heavy work needed to prepare for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: because of the exertion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer, from עולא. Preparing a wedding takes a lot of effort, and heavy work is not fitting on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason has nothing to do with joy at all. It connects the ban to the general idea of limiting work on חול המועד, which is the main topic of this מסכת.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
because of the exertion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to step 22's question, not based on joy.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wedding preparations are too much work for חול המועד.

steps.title: Fourth answer: people would delay having children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא says the ban prevents people from delaying weddings until the festival, which would hold back פריה ורביה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא said: because of the neglect of פריה ורביה (having children).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a fourth answer. If weddings were allowed on the festival, people might wait for the festival to marry, and that delay would hold up having children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason looks at what would happen in society if weddings were allowed. People could save money by using one feast for both the festival and the wedding, so they would push off marrying. The rabbis banned it so that people would not delay the מצוה of פריה ורביה.
steps.whatToRemember: Four reasons for the ban: (1) do not mix joys, (2) the festival's joy would be pushed aside (רב, from בחגך), (3) too much work, (4) people would delay having children.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa said:
because of the neglect of being fruitful and multiplying.
phrases.notes: The idea is that people would wait for the festival to marry, to save on a separate feast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth, separate answer to step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Allowing festival weddings would lead people to delay marriage and so delay פריה ורביה.

steps.title: A ברייתא is brought to challenge the reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that talks about all those who are forbidden to marry on the festival, to challenge one of the reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: All those whom they said are forbidden to marry on the festival —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It starts quoting a ברייתא, and the rest of the ברייתא and the challenge continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיתיבי tells us that a source is about to be used against one of the reasons just given. We do not yet know which reason is being attacked. That becomes clear once the ברייתא is finished.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
All those whom they said
are forbidden to marry on the festival —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a ברייתא to challenge one of the reasons in steps 23–27.
steps.kashyaTarget: One of the reasons given for the ban on festival weddings (made clear in the continuation).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about those forbidden to marry on the festival will be shown to clash with one of the reasons. The rest of the ברייתא and the challenge come on the next amud.
